page: Microsoft Azure F16as_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Fasv6 server family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The server features 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs running at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz, with 1.0 thread per core. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The CPU cache configuration includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache. This instance does not include any GPUs or local storage, though it is Premium Storage capable. Virtualization is managed via the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

In benchmark evaluations, the F16as_v6 demonstrates strong single-core performance, scoring in the top 25% for stress-ng single-core CPU tests and Geekbench single-core metrics. Multi-core performance is also strong, as evidenced by Geekbench multi-core results, though stress-ng multi-core performance falls into the average tier. The processor's instruction set capabilities, including AVX-512 and cryptographic acceleration, support efficient operations. Notably, text processing benchmarks place this server in the top 10% tier. Memory performance is robust, with a strong PassMark memory score and average uncached read and write memory bandwidths of 75.97 GB/sec and 56.09 GB/sec, respectively. For language model workloads, the server achieves top-tier text generation speeds of 349.71 tokens/sec on small 135M models, while maintaining average performance on larger 7B and 70B models.

The absence of bundled local storage represents a key architectural tradeoff, requiring reliance on external Premium Storage options for data persistence. From a cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated AMD EPYC cores and balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio offer a solid resource density for workloads that do not require GPU acceleration. This configuration is well-suited for general-purpose computing, text processing, software compilation, web serving, and lightweight machine learning inference tasks.
